source.title: Constructed exercise (not from a publication): a methane throttling valve from 50 bar to 20 bar
source.note: every input is my choice, flagged assumed. The topic comes from the IIT Kharagpur NPTEL course plan (Principles and Practices of Process Equipment and Plant Design, week 10: plant hydraulics, pumps and compressors); the lectures are videos and their transcripts could not be reached, so none of their content or numbers is used

reported.name: outlet_T
reported.anchor: independent: isenthalpic expansion (constant enthalpy) with CoolProp methane, so the real-gas Joule-Thomson cooling

reported.name: outlet_vapor_fraction
reported.anchor: methane at 25 C and below 50 bar is a gas

tolerance.note: outlet temperature 5 percent (of the value in C; the real cooling is about 12 K so this is about 0.6 K), fixed before the run; the paper package is my assumption and Raoult's Law is listed to show that an ideal gas has no Joule-Thomson effect

scenarios.why: throttled only to 30 bar: less cooling (independent calculation)

review.method: independent isentropic and isenthalpic calculations with CoolProp
